metadata.title: Survey of Adult Skills 2023 – Country Notes: Japan

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The Survey of Adult Skills 2023 uses a household survey design with a sample drawn to be representative of the target population of adults aged 16–65 in Japan (about 74.7 million adults), irrespective of nationality, citizenship, or language status. The country notes report an overall response rate (41%) and state that analyses were conducted to ensure that non-response does not introduce significant bias, implying the use of survey design adjustments/weighting procedures even though the specific weight variable names are not provided in the excerpt. The assessment proficiency scales are derived from performance on digital tasks administered on tablets, and results are reported with uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals), consistent with complex survey estimation. No machine-learning model is trained here, so there is no ML-specific omission of weights; however, the exact weight and replicate-weight methodology is not documented in the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country note describing descriptive results and associations from the Survey of Adult Skills, not an empirical predictive modeling study that reports how plausible values (PVs) or missing data were handled in model estimation. The proficiency estimates are reported on 500-point scales and by proficiency levels, but the excerpt does not specify whether PVs were used, how they were combined, or what missing-data strategy was applied in the underlying OECD scaling model. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Japan country note for Survey of Adult Skills 2023 (cycle 2022–23). The analytic sample consists of adults aged 16–65 who participated in the survey in Japan; the excerpt does not describe additional analytic exclusions beyond the general survey design. The note also states that doorstep questionnaire respondents (offered when respondents were not sufficiently fluent in the assessment language) are generally excluded when comparing across cycles to maximize comparability, but it does not specify whether doorstep respondents are included in the specific reported comparisons in this excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: The OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 assesses adults aged 16–65 in Japan (2022–23 cycle) using a personal interview plus a self-completed assessment administered exclusively on digital devices (tablets). Proficiency in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—is estimated on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels based on task success/failure, with uncertainty reported via 95% confidence intervals. In Japan, mean performance is above the OECD average in all three domains (literacy 289, numeracy 291, adaptive problem solving 276). The note reports the distribution across proficiency levels (e.g., 10% at or below Level 1 in literacy and numeracy; 11% at or below Level 1 in adaptive problem solving) and highlights age-related gaps (older adults 55–65 scoring lower than 25–34 year-olds). It also documents associations between higher numeracy proficiency and better employment outcomes (including a reported 10% higher wages per one standard-deviation increase in numeracy among employed adults, after accounting for other differences), while emphasizing that these are descriptive/associational results rather than causal estimates.
